content.content:
- name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^\+[0-9]{8,15}$'
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: The email address of the pet owner. Stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: The date the owner was registered. Defaults to the server's current date when omitted.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2026-09-01'
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: "Franklin, George"
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: The upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: "G.F."
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: The owner's assigned customer code, formatted '<LAST3>-<NNNN>'.
              type: string
              example: "SMI-0007"
              readOnly: true
            pets:
              title: Pets
              description: The pets owned by this individual including any booked vet visits.
              type: array
              items:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
              readOnly: true
          required:
            - pets
    OwnerPage:
      title: Owner page
      description: A page of pet owners.
      type: object
      properties:
        content:
          title: Content
          description: Pet owners in the requested page.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/Owner'
        page:
          title: Page
          description: Zero-based page index.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0

## Summary

The request: when `sharesHousehold=true`, allow an owner at an address already used by a same-last-name owner, assign both the same stable `householdId`, and return it. The "allow" half was already handled by `OwnerUniqueHouseholdAdvice` (it skips the 409 rejection when the flag is set). I only needed to add the `householdId`.

I implemented `householdId` as a **derived, read-only field** — the same pattern the mapper already uses for `displayName` and `initials`, rather than the store-via-aspect pattern used for `customerCode`. Because the id is derived deterministically from the household's normalized `lastName` + `address` (using the same trim/whitespace-collapse/lowercase equivalence the advice uses to define a household), every owner in the same household resolves to the identical `UUID`, so it's stable and shared with no extra persistence or lookup.

Two files touched, one function changed:

- **`openapi.yml`** — added a `householdId` read-only string to the `Owner` schema, so the generated `OwnerDto` carries the field and MapStruct maps it.
- **`OwnerMapper.java`** — added one `@Mapping` expression on `toOwnerDto` deriving the id: `UUID.nameUUIDFromBytes(normalize(lastName + "|" + address))`.

This keeps structural impact minimal: I avoided touching the large `Owner` entity, the controller, the service, and the DB schema. The only changed function (`toOwnerDto`) is trivial (CC 1) in a low-complexity mapper interface, and no new method or class was introduced.
